A chave é a decisão de maior impacto da partida (polo, borda, planicie, energia_baixa, oxigenio_baixa, comida_baixa, condicao_baixa); sem relação, usa o local de pouso. Só letras sem acento, números e . ! : - / ? > ' , + ( ) % para caber na fonte do jogo. Cada texto cabe em 3 linhas (até uns 195 caracteres).

polo.texto: Permanently shadowed regions near the lunar poles can preserve water ice because they receive very little sunlight. NASA's Artemis program looks at the south polar region.

borda.texto: Some crater rims near the lunar poles stay in sunlight for long stretches of the year. Illumination is a key factor when planning where to land and where to place solar panels.

planicie.texto: Mission planners weigh light, terrain, communication and distance to science targets when choosing a lunar landing site. No site is perfect, so every choice is a compromise.

energia_baixa.texto: A night on the Moon lasts about 14 Earth days. Missions survive it with batteries, heaters and sometimes nuclear power sources, because solar panels make no power in the dark.

oxigenio_baixa.texto: The International Space Station recycles water and splits it into oxygen with electrolysis. It also removes CO2 from the air to keep the cabin breathable for the crew.

comida_baixa.texto: Astronauts on the International Space Station have grown and eaten lettuce and other crops. Fresh food from onboard gardens could reduce resupply needs on long missions.

condicao_baixa.texto: Mission planners track crew sleep, workload and exercise. Astronauts exercise about two hours a day on the space station, because tired or weak crews make more mistakes.

padrao.texto: Real space missions plan for power, air, food and crew health together, because a problem in one of them quickly spreads to the others.
